title: bounty.index — every public bounty, one index
excerpt: Every public bug bounty program across five platforms — filterable by scope, payout, and asset type.
content_html:
§01/Workflow

Three steps.
Zero platform-hopping.

01step

Aggregate.

Every public program from five platforms pulled daily into a single normalized index. HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack, Federacy.

// source · arkadiyt/bounty-targets-data

02step

Filter.

Platform, asset type (wildcard, API, mobile, hardware, source), minimum payout tier, and full-text scope search. Chip-based. URL is the state.

// scan-heavy · not click-heavy

03step

Hunt.

Open a program to see full in-scope + out-of-scope lists with severity notes. Jump straight to the platform to submit.

// / to search · j k ↵

§02/Why this exists

Every alternative is fragmented.

Each platform shows its own programs. Directories are stale or policy-only. Raw JSON is fine if you enjoy jq. And none of them speak MCP. This is the one built for scanning — by you or your agent.

§03/What it does

Four things.
Done properly.

02 · lookup

Scope lookup

Paste a domain. Instant verdict — in-scope somewhere, or not.

$ lookup tesla.com

→ in scope · 2 programs

/scope-lookup

03 · nav

Keyboard-first

/searchj kmove↵openescblur

anywhere

04 · feed

Log & RSS

New programs surface within an hour, grouped as a dated log. Subscribe by RSS or read the web view.

/feed
